# Deliverable A
```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 10
%%| fig-height: 4.7
%%| out-width: 90%
classDiagram
    direction LR

    class Message {
        +str sender
        +str role
        +str content
    }

    class LLMClient {
        +str model
        +complete(messages) str
    }

    class Tool {
        <<interface>>
        +str name
        +run(args) str
    }

    class ReadTicket {
        +run(ticket_id) str
    }
    class ReadRoster {
        +run(engineer_id) None
    }
    class WriteRoster {
        +run(ticket_id, engineer_id) None
    }
    class KnowledgeBaseLookup {
        +run(query) str
    }

    class Agent {
        +str name
        +str system_prompt
        +LLMClient llm
        +dict tools
        +act(transcript) Message
    }

    class Orchestrator {
        +dict agents
        +list transcript
        +ask(name, prompt) Message
        +reach_consensus(...) Message
        +run() None
    }
    
    class Roster {
        +engineers: List[Engineer]
    }

    class Engineer {
        +str name
        +str specialty
        +int capacity_remaining
    }


    Tool <|.. ReadTicket : Triager
    Tool <|.. WriteRoster : Dispatcher ONLY
    Tool <|.. KnowledgeBaseLookup : Triager
    Tool <|.. ReadRoster : Reviewer

    Agent --> LLMClient : uses
    Agent --> Tool : holds many
    Orchestrator --> Agent : coordinates 3
    Orchestrator --> Message : owns transcript
    Roster --> Engineer
    ReadRoster --> Roster : reads
    WriteRoster --> Roster : writes
```

# Deliverable B
```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 10
%%| fig-height: 7
%%| out-width: 90%
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant O as Orchestrator
    participant T as Triager
    participant R as Reviewer
    participant D as Dispatcher
    participant L as LLMClient
    participant Tool as Tool
    participant Ro as Roster

    O->>T: run(ticket_id)

    T->>L: complete(system_prompt + ticket_id)
    L-->>T: "TOOL: ReadTicket"
    T->>Tool: execute ReadTicket(ticket_id)
    Tool-->>T: ticket summary

    T->>L: complete(system_prompt + ticket summary)
    L-->>T: "TOOL: KnowledgeBaseLookup"
    T->>Tool: execute KnowledgeBaseLookup(query)
    Tool-->>T: knowledge summary

    T->>L: generate proposal
    L-->>T: category, severity, suggested_engineer
    T-->>O: proposal

    loop Until reviewer approves or max rounds reached
        O->>R: review proposal

        R->>L: complete(review_prompt + proposal)
        L-->>R: "TOOL: ReadRoster"
        R->>Tool: execute ReadRoster()
        Tool-->>R: roster state

        R->>L: complete(review_prompt + roster state)
        L-->>R: approve or critique
        R-->>O: reviewer result

        alt Reviewer rejects
            O->>T: critique + previous proposal
            T->>L: revise proposal
            L-->>T: revised proposal
            T-->>O: revised proposal
        else Reviewer approves
            O->>D: final approved proposal
        end
    end

    D->>L: complete(dispatch_prompt + final proposal)
    L-->>D: "TOOL: WriteRoster"
    D->>Tool: execute WriteRoster(ticket_id, engineer_id)
    Tool->>Ro: update assignment and capacity
    Ro-->>Tool: success
    Tool-->>D: dispatch result
    D-->>O: final assignment
```

# Deliverable C
```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 10
%%| fig-height: 6.7
%%| out-width: 90%

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber

    participant O as Orchestrator
    participant T as Triager
    participant R as Reviewer
    participant D as Dispatcher
    participant L as LLMClient
    participant Tool as Tool
    participant Ro as Roster

    Note over O,R: PARALLEL REGION — runs concurrently for each Ticket N

    par Ticket N
        O->>T: run(Ticket N)

        T->>L: analyze Ticket N
        L-->>T: TOOL: ReadTicket
        T->>Tool: ReadTicket(Ticket N)
        Tool-->>T: ticket data

        T->>L: analyze ticket + context
        L-->>T: TOOL: KnowledgeBaseLookup
        T->>Tool: KnowledgeBaseLookup(query)
        Tool-->>T: KB results

        T->>L: generate proposal
        L-->>T: category, severity, suggested_engineer
        T-->>O: Proposal N

        O->>R: Review Proposal N

        R->>L: inspect proposal
        L-->>R: TOOL: ReadRoster
        R->>Tool: ReadRoster()
        Tool->>Ro: read roster
        Ro-->>Tool: specialties + capacities
        Tool-->>R: roster data

        R->>L: critique proposal
        L-->>R: approve / reject
        R-->>O: review result

        loop Until approved or max rounds reached
            alt Reviewer rejects
                O->>T: critique + previous proposal
                T->>L: revise proposal
                L-->>T: revised proposal
                T-->>O: revised Proposal N

                O->>R: review revised proposal
                R-->>O: approve / reject
            else Reviewer approves
                Note over O,R: Proposal N ready for dispatch
            end
        end
    end

    Note over O,Ro: SERIAL JOIN — dispatch one ticket at a time

    loop For each approved Ticket N
        O->>D: Dispatch Proposal N

        D->>L: commit assignment
        L-->>D: TOOL: WriteRoster
        D->>Tool: WriteRoster(ticket_id, engineer_id)

        Tool->>Ro: check capacity + assign + decrement
        Ro-->>Tool: success / failure
        Tool-->>D: AssignmentResult

        D-->>O: dispatch result
    end
```

# Deliverable D
## Question 1
I would allow the Triager to execute proposals in parallel as tickets are independent of each other. Additionally, the Reviewer can then independently check for the proposal's severity, duplicaticity, specialty fit, and availability. These steps can be done in parallel because they are read only operations. For the serial join, I'd reconcile the Triager and Reviewer's outputs and have the Dispatcher update the Roster. This must be done sequentially because of the race condition that exists if capacity remaining is being decremented.

## Question 2
The shared mutable state is the Roster, or more specifically, the Engineer's capacity remaining. The arbiter is the Dispatcher, which is the only agent allowed to mutate the roster. Without the arbiter, two tickets could be assigned to a specific engineer with one slot left, essentially making the capacity remaining negative and over assigning that specific engineer. My design prevents this by only approving tickets through the Dispatcher serially.

## Question 3
The Traiger's single duty is proposing the ticket's category, severity, and suggested_engineer with tools ReadTicket and KnowledgeBaseLookup. The Reviewer's single duty is to critique the Triager's proposal and verify that the proposed engineer has the right specialty and available capacity with tool ReadRoster.  The Dispatcher's single duty is to commit the approved assignment to shared state with the tool WriteRoster. 

If you let the Triager also use the Dispatcher's functionality, it could automatically commit its proposal without letting the Reviewer check first.

## Question 4
Add an Escalator agent with a prompt stating that "If severity == 1 and no qualified engineer has capacity, page a human responder, otherwise do nothing". Give it the ReadRoster tool and a PageHuman tool. Have the agent take the Reviewer's output and if there is a qualified engineer, go as planned, and if not, page human. I wouldn't modify the current Roster class as it has everything you need.

## Final Question
Something that I took away from this lab is that multi-agent design is indeed much more complex than a single agent. What I found impactful about multi-agent systems is the ability to divvy up your work amongst different agents and how it affects verification of work, safer tool calls, scaling, debugging, etc.
